logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, while creating a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) restricted to eligible products, confirm an assignment of catalogue items such as a category, collection or product. The entire discount editor is replaced by an unexpected-error screen instead of retaining the selected items and allowing setup to continue. The trigger is confirming eligibility assignment on a new voucher, separately from applying filters inside an assignment dialog.
logicalBugs.rootCause: VoucherCreatePage unconditionally maps the active catalogue tab through mapLocalVariantsToSavedVariants, whose mapper dereferences variant.product. Category and collection objects, and product objects themselves, are not variant-shaped; switching to these assigned-item tabs can therefore throw after assignment. This cause does not establish a crash for a correctly shaped variant or a filter submission.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, while creating a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) restricted to eligible products, confirm an assignment of catalogue items such as a category, collection or product. The entire discount editor is replaced by an unexpected-error screen instead of retaining the selected items and allowing setup to continue. The trigger is confirming eligibility assignment on a new voucher, separately from applying filters inside an assignment dialog.

logicalBugs.description: A Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) is a discount redeemable using its codes. On a new, unsaved voucher, the setup checklist counts locally added codes twice: one manual code is reported as two ready codes, and generated draft codes are similarly doubled. The code table and saved voucher contain the actual number, so the defect is the readiness count rather than duplicate code creation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getVoucherSetupReadiness adds listedCodesCount and draftCodesCount when no saved total exists; the client list already includes the same draft codes.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a new voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), manually add one code or generate a batch without saving. The setup checklist reports twice as many ready codes as the code table contains; after saving, only the actual code rows exist, confirming a checklist overcount rather than duplicate creation.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, on phone/tablet voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) forms, setup shortcuts and section navigation fail to reveal their destination. Add codes, Set value, Usage limits, Codes and Requirements can leave the viewport unchanged or jump to the page top, requiring manual scrolling despite an available section target.
logicalBugs.rootCause: All setup and navigation actions call scrollElementIntoDetailContent, which selects the marked detail root and computes scrolling only within it. At mobile/tablet breakpoints where the effective document scroll owner differs, scrolling that root cannot reveal the requested section.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at phone width on a new voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), click Add codes in the setup checklist. The view stays on the checklist instead of scrolling to the existing Voucher codes section, requiring manual scrolling to reach it.

In Saleor, at phone width on a new voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), click Set value in the setup checklist. The discount value field remains below the screen instead of being scrolled into view, so the shortcut does not take the admin to the field it names.

In Saleor, at tablet width while creating a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), click Codes in the section navigation. The page jumps to its top instead of bringing the Voucher codes section into view.

In Saleor, at tablet width on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), select Requirements in the section navigation. Earlier sections remain visible and Minimum Requirements stays offscreen instead of becoming the visible destination.

In Saleor, at phone width on the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) setup checklist, click the Usage limits shortcut under Worth reviewing. The screen stays on the checklist while the Usage limits section remains farther down the form.

In Saleor, at tablet width on a Products-scope voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), return to the top after saving and refreshing, then click Eligible products in the section navigation. That item becomes highlighted but the page still shows Details and Voucher codes instead of scrolling to the eligibility section.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor’s voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) list, clicking the Name sort does not order rows by the visible voucher names. The order follows voucher codes instead, so the displayed Name column appears incorrectly sorted.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The displayed code column renders rowData.name, but getSortQueryField maps its sort key to VoucherSortField.CODE instead of NAME.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor’s Vouchers list, click the Name column to sort descending. The active indicator changes, but the displayed voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) names are not in descending name order; the order follows their codes rather than the names shown in that column.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, a failed voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) Save can still persist part of the edit: a new name or discount type can survive a rejected sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) discount, and deleting an existing code can succeed while its duplicate replacement is rejected. Returning to the list and choosing Ignore changes does not undo those already committed edits.
logicalBugs.rootCause: createUpdateHandler starts voucherUpdate, voucherChannelListingUpdate, code deletion and catalogue updates as independent promises and waits for Promise.all only after they have started. Errors are collected after independent commits, without a transaction, preflight barrier or compensation. The same orchestration produces metadata/channel partial writes and code replacement partial deletion; type changes can also race channel validation against the old discount type.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with fixed monetary discounts in multiple sales channels (storefront/currency configurations), switch the discount type to Percentage and enter an amount above the allowed percentage maximum for one channel. Save can report success and retain that invalid percentage instead of rejecting the type-and-value change consistently.

In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), edit its name and enter an invalid percentage above the allowed maximum in one sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration), then Save. The discount is rejected but the name has already persisted, without clear feedback that only part of the requested change was saved.

In Saleor, on a saved free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), switch to an entire-order discount and submit a sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) value that is rejected. The failed save still changes the voucher’s discount scope/type, and reopening can show an unintended full order discount instead of preserving the original shipping configuration.

In Saleor, replacing voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) A’s existing code with a code already used by voucher B reports a failed Save, but A’s staged code deletion still persists. Choosing Back > Ignore changes and reopening A reveals that its original active code is gone.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, if a new code-redeemable discount voucher’s sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) discount is rejected, such as an excessive percentage or a missing fixed amount, creation can still persist the voucher and reserve its code. Correcting the discount then fails with a duplicate-code error, leaving an incomplete voucher despite the failed creation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: createHandler first creates the voucher and its codes, then separately updates channel listings. A channel error is returned without deleting/rolling back the already-created voucher, leaving an active incomplete record.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, a failed 120% voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) save still creates a voucher with one code and no sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) discount; correcting the percentage then fails because that code already exists.

In Saleor, during creation of a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with a unique manual code, submit a fixed discount with one required sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) amount missing. Correct that amount and Save again; creation is now blocked by a code-already-exists error because the first rejected attempt already reserved the code.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor’s voucher list with All sales channels (storefront/currency configurations) selected, vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes) with channel-specific minimum order values show a blank minimum-spend cell. The list provides neither a shared value nor a Varies by channel summary, hiding an existing minimum-spend requirement.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The min-spent cell looks up the selected channel and renders its value; when channels exist but none is selected it passes null to moneyCell without summarizing equal values or Varies by channel.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor’s Vouchers list, leave the channel selector on All sales channels (storefront/currency configurations) while a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) has saved channel-specific minimum order amounts. Its Min. Spent cell is blank instead of showing a common value or indicating that the requirements differ by channel.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, at phone width, voucher-list search/filter controls exceed the viewport and can shift the content pane sideways. The shifted empty-results view clips "No vouchers found", and selecting vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes) can leave the bulk Delete vouchers action offscreen.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ListFilters puts a fixed 360px search field plus filter controls and actions in an auto/1fr grid without a responsive stacked alternative, widening the page and pushing bulk actions out of view.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at 390px, edit voucher search until the overwide search field shifts the content pane sideways, then search for a value with no matches. The empty-results view retains the horizontal offset, clipping "No vouchers found" as well as the search controls.

In Saleor, at phone width, select vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes) in the list to expose bulk actions. The overwide search/filter toolbar leaves Delete vouchers offscreen instead of keeping that bulk action accessible for the selected rows.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s Assign Countries dialog, the select-all checkbox says "Select all channels" although the rows and the operation concern countries. The reused label misidentifies what selecting all will change.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DiscountCountrySelectDialog renders ChannelsAvailabilitySelectAll directly without overriding its channel terminology for countries.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, open Assign countries for a free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes). The select-all checkbox says “Select all channels,” although checking it selects the country rows, misidentifying the items the action changes.

logicalBugs.description: Saleor’s Vouchers list has a Percentage filter intended to show percentage-off discounts. Applying it also returns a free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), and the unrelated result remains after refresh instead of being excluded as a different discount type.
logicalBugs.rootCause: filter_discount_type filters PERCENTAGE only by discount_value_type; shipping vouchers also store percentage type and are not excluded by their voucher type.
reproductionPaths: Saleor’s Vouchers list has a Percentage filter intended to show percentage-off discounts. Applying it also returns a free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), and the unrelated result remains after refresh instead of being excluded as a different discount type.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, opening the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) availability chooser displays the title "Manage Products Channel Availability". The modal is editing voucher availability, so its product-specific title misidentifies the object being changed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: VoucherCreate supplies the copied Manage Products Channel Availability title to the shared channel dialog rather than voucher-specific copy.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, open Manage availability for a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) to choose the sales channels (storefront/currency configurations) where the discount is offered. The dialog title reads “Manage Products Channel Availability,” incorrectly describing product availability instead of voucher availability.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, a saved free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with no country restrictions displays "Voucher is limited to these countries" immediately above "Voucher applies to all countries". The same empty country selection is described as both restricted and worldwide.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The country section uses empty countries for the worldwide state while also rendering its restricted-country explanatory description, so the two independent text paths contradict one another.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, save a free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) without any country restriction, then inspect its country section. It simultaneously says the voucher is limited to selected countries and applies to all countries, giving contradictory descriptions of the same empty/worldwide selection.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, voucher Save can report "Voucher updated" while retaining a false unsaved draft and leave-page warning. This occurs after turning off a populated requirement/end-date control, saving a zero minimum spend, or clearing a schedule date that the server defaults or leaves unset. Reload shows the stored canonical settings and clears the warning.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The detail form uses useForm with useStateFromProps and its merge function. That merge replaces a local field only when the incoming initial field differs from its previous server value. Saving a normalized value that is unchanged on the server therefore retains the changed local toggle/text, including disabled fields, zero-requirement selections and blank defaulted dates. No successful-save reset reconciles the whole form with canonical persisted values.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), fill a requirement or end-date field and then switch that feature off before saving. Save succeeds, but the now-inactive field values keep the form marked unsaved and produce a leave-page warning instead of reconciling the editor with the saved disabled state.

In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), enable a minimum order value or item quantity and save zero as the minimum. Save reports success, but the editor retains the zero-valued enabled draft and an unsaved General settings warning; reopening shows the stored disabled requirement with a clean form.

In Saleor’s voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) schedule, after clearing an existing current-day Start Date, Save correctly stores today’s default but the editor keeps the date blank and reports unsaved Schedule changes. With an initially absent end date, saving a cleared End Date similarly leaves Set end date checked although no end date is stored. Successful Save should display the stored defaults, as initial creation does.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), Save can proceed while a minimum item quantity or total usage limit displays a validation error. Rejected minimum quantities, including zero or an integer too large to store, can show a green Voucher updated toast beside an error, Try again, or unsaved state; zero-valued controls can also reopen disabled.
logicalBugs.rootCause: VoucherRequirements and VoucherLimits calculate invalid minimum quantity/usage-limit flags only for inline display. The shared createVoucherUpdateHandler gates submit using validateChannelListing and buildChannelListingLocalErrors, which contain neither of those non-channel checks. Consequently those displayed invalid fields reach the same submit path as valid data. This explains the missing submit gate for local quantity/limit errors. It does not prove why a server-rejected large quantity shows success: at the pinned revision VoucherDetails.handleSubmit collects mutation errors before notifying success, so that notification mechanism remains unresolved. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), enable a total usage limit and replace a saved positive limit with zero. Save proceeds despite the minimum-one error; after reload the cap control is off even though the stored usage limit remains zero rather than unset.

In Saleor, when the minimum quantity of items is rejected, for example 0 or a value too large to store such as 2147483648, Save still shows a green Voucher updated toast while the error, a Try again button or the unsaved General settings indicator remains.

On a Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with a saved positive minimum item quantity, replace that quantity with zero and blur to show the minimum-one error. Save nevertheless reports Voucher updated and turns the saved requirement off, removing its input instead of retaining the prior requirement for correction.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, delete vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes) in bulk from the Vouchers list, then leave and return to that list. Already deleted rows briefly reappear before the refreshed results remove them, making completed deletions look undone; the report does not claim those vouchers are recreated on the server.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Bulk deletion refetches the active list but does not evict deleted entities from all cached variable variants, allowing navigation to show an old cached result before the network refresh.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, delete vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes) in bulk from the Vouchers list, then leave and return to that list. Already deleted rows briefly reappear before the refreshed results remove them, making completed deletions look undone; the report does not claim those vouchers are recreated on the server.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, revisiting the saved detail URL of a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) deleted through the list leaves the page on loading skeletons even after the lookup completes with no voucher. A fresh revisit produces the same terminal state.
logicalBugs.rootCause: VoucherDetailsPage reveals the layout only when voucher exists and codes loading settles; a completed null lookup never sets revealedForVoucherId or renders a not-found state.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, revisiting the saved detail URL of a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) deleted through the list leaves the page on loading skeletons even after the lookup completes with no voucher. A fresh revisit produces the same terminal state.

logicalBugs.description: A Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) can be limited to particular product variants, such as an item’s specific size. Its assigned-variants table labels both the product-name and product-type columns Product Name, leaving two different kinds of values under indistinguishable headings instead of identifying each property.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DiscountVariants assigns discountVariantsTableProductHeader to both the product name and type columns instead of a product-type label.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved Products-scope voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), open its assigned product variants table. Both the product-name and product-type columns have the heading Product Name, even though the values beneath them represent different properties.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, on a new unsaved Products-scope voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), assign more product variants than fit on one table page. The form reports the full assigned count but Next remains disabled, preventing access to the remaining rows. Increasing the page size reveals them, so they were assigned successfully and the failure is draft-table pagination.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The create page spreads specificItemsPagination into PaginatorContext, leaving hasNextPage/hasPreviousPage nested under pageInfo; consumer controls read flattened flags and remain disabled despite another local page.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a new unsaved Products-scope voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), assign enough product variants to need a second table page. Only the first page is displayed and Next remains disabled, so the remaining assigned variants cannot be reached through pagination.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, removing the only assigned variant or all voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) codes on the last page can leave the voucher editor displaying an empty table with no usable pagination, although earlier pages still contain items. Saving does not necessarily recover the list; reload reveals the surviving variants/codes.
logicalBugs.rootCause: useLocalPageInfo resets page only when paginateBy changes, not when values shrink below its current page. Removing final-page variants or codes leaves pageValues as an empty out-of-range slice.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved Products-scope voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), go to the last page of assigned variants and unassign its only remaining variant. The table becomes empty and its pagination disappears even though earlier pages still contain assigned variants, making those surviving items unreachable until recovery.

In Saleor, on a saved code-redeemable discount voucher’s codes table, delete all codes on the final page while earlier pages still contain codes. The editor stays on an empty table with no pagination, even after a successful Save; reload reveals the surviving codes.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s Add code > Manual code dialog, confirm without entering a code. The dialog accepts the empty value and shows a blank Draft row instead of generating or rejecting a code before confirmation. Only saving the whole voucher replaces that blank row with a generated code the admin could not review in the draft.
logicalBugs.rootCause: generateDraftVoucherCode stores its supplied string directly, and manual confirmation permits an empty code; only API creation trims/generates a replacement later, leaving a blank draft until Save.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s Add code > Manual code dialog, confirm without entering a code. The dialog accepts the empty value and shows a blank Draft row instead of generating or rejecting a code before confirmation. Only saving the whole voucher replaces that blank row with a generated code the admin could not review in the draft.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, at phone width on an existing voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), the detail header squeezes its status badge beside the title and actions. The Active label is visibly clipped instead of remaining fully readable, even though the voucher’s detail page otherwise opens normally.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The TopNav/detail header retains title/status/action row widths without enough nonshrinking room for the Active badge at 390px.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at phone width on an existing voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), the detail header squeezes its status badge beside the title and actions. The Active label is visibly clipped instead of remaining fully readable, even though the voucher’s detail page otherwise opens normally.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, at phone width, save changes in the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) editor. The success or error notification extends beyond the screen edge, clipping the feedback that should explain the result of the save instead of keeping the message readable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The toast stylesheet sets width:380px independently of viewport width; placement in the notification viewport adds an inset, exceeding a 390px screen.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at phone width, save changes in the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) editor. The success or error notification extends beyond the screen edge, clipping the feedback that should explain the result of the save instead of keeping the message readable.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, voucher minimum item quantity and total usage limit accept fractional values such as 1.5 or 7.5 without an integer validation message. Save can silently truncate the displayed quantity/cap to an integer, while an existing code-redeemable discount voucher’s edited cap can remain displayed as a fractional number of redemptions.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The quantity and usage-limit number controls validate minimum/range conditions but do not enforce Number.isInteger or an equivalent integer-domain input contract before submit. Handlers forward parseFloat quantity and numeric usage-limit values to integer API/model fields; detail state/display can retain the submitted fraction while creation/storage normalizes it. These are the same missing integer-domain validation exposed through distinct create/edit fields.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, in a new code-redeemable discount voucher’s minimum-item requirement, enter a fractional quantity and Save. The field accepts and displays the fraction without integer validation, but the saved quantity becomes a smaller whole number instead of matching the accepted displayed value.

In Saleor, in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s total Limit of Uses field, enter a fractional cap and Save. The displayed fraction is accepted without integer validation, but reopening shows the cap truncated to a whole number instead of the value that appeared to save.

In Saleor, on an existing voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), enter a fractional total Limit of Uses and save it. The detail page reports a fractional number of redemptions left, although uses are discrete whole redemption events.

logicalBugs.description: A Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) whose redemption limit is exhausted appears in Expired results but is still labeled Active because the badge checks dates alone. With current valid dates and a zero total limit, the row shows 0 of 0 and Active even though no redemptions remain; the status should reflect the exhausted limit.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Status labels derive promotion/schedule phase from startDate and endDate only, without incorporating usageLimit versus used; exhausted vouchers therefore still read Active.
reproductionPaths: A Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) whose redemption limit is exhausted appears in Expired results but is still labeled Active because the badge checks dates alone. With current valid dates and a zero total limit, the row shows 0 of 0 and Active even though no redemptions remain; the status should reflect the exhausted limit.

logicalBugs.description: On a Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) schedule, partly clearing a start or end time leaves some entered time segments visible. Save succeeds but replaces that incomplete time with midnight, discarding the remaining entered hours or minutes instead of asking for a complete time. A genuinely blank optional time defaulting to midnight is a separate, accepted behavior.
logicalBugs.rootCause: joinDateTime falls back to 00:00 for falsy time input. The partially entered native time control produces an empty value that is silently replaced instead of rejected.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s Start Hour field, leave the hour and minutes filled but remove the AM/PM segment. Saving succeeds and changes the time to midnight instead of preserving the entered time or asking the admin to complete it.

In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with an enabled expiry, clear only the hour segment of End Hour while leaving minutes and AM/PM visible. Saving reports success and replaces the expiry time with midnight, which persists after reload instead of rejecting the incomplete time.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, a code-redeemable discount voucher’s schedule can have an end time earlier than its start time on the same day. Save correctly rejects that chronology, but error styling marks only End Date and leaves End Hour looking valid, even though the hour is what needs correction. The issue is the missing time-field indication, not the validity of the rejection or the wording “End date cannot be before the start date.”
logicalBugs.rootCause: DiscountDates maps the API endDate DateTime error to the End Date control and explicitly does not paint it onto End Hour, even when time order causes the failure.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor’s voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) schedule, a same-day end of 09:30 before a 10:00 start is correctly rejected, but only End Date has error styling. End Hour remains visually valid even though changing that hour resolves the conflict.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor’s Vouchers list, delete the only voucher on the final page while earlier pages still contain vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes). The empty result keeps an enabled Previous button that does nothing, leaving no working pagination route back to the surviving records until the list is reset through navigation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Voucher list deletion refetches with the existing cursor and keeps pagination anchored to the deleted page instead of navigating to a valid page; an empty edge list cannot supply the cursor for previous navigation.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, deleting the only voucher on page 2 leaves an empty list with an enabled Previous button that does nothing. The surviving vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes) remain accessible after resetting the list through navigation.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, at phone width, voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) Status filters and collection-assignment filters clip their required value selector outside the filter panel. Apply can remain disabled because the control needed to complete the filter cannot be reached normally.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ConditionalFilter rows lay out condition/operator/value controls within the narrow panel and apply overflow:hidden to valueField. The selector can be pushed outside its available width and then clipped.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at a 390px viewport, selecting Status in voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) Filters clips the required value selector outside the panel, leaving Apply disabled and preventing normal touch interaction with the filter.

In Saleor, at phone width, open a code-redeemable discount voucher’s collection-assignment dialog and configure a filter that requires a value. Its value selector is clipped outside the filter panel, preventing normal completion of the filter even though the filter choice is offered.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, search the Vouchers list and choose a descending sort, then open one of the matching vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes). Clicking the detail page’s Back button returns to an unfiltered, ascending-sorted list instead of restoring the search and ordering from which that voucher was opened.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The detail backlink depends on history.state.prevLocation; navigation paths lacking that state, including plain row anchors, fall back to voucherListPath without the originating query.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, search the Vouchers list and choose a descending sort, then open one of the matching vouchers (discounts redeemed using codes). Clicking the detail page’s Back button returns to an unfiltered, ascending-sorted list instead of restoring the search and ordering from which that voucher was opened.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, saving a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with a total usage limit that is empty or outside the accepted integer range can show a green "Voucher updated" toast alongside Try again and an unsaved-changes warning. The invalid limit remains unsaved, so success and failure feedback contradict each other.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The report establishes contradictory success and failed-save feedback for an invalid usage limit. The pinned createUpdateHandler returns all mutation errors and VoucherDetails.handleSubmit only calls notifySaved when that array is empty; the previously proposed independent per-mutation toast mechanism is not supported by this source. A missing/empty returned error payload or timing/state discrepancy is a candidate, but the exact cause is unresolved without execution evidence. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, with the total usage limit enabled, saving an empty limit (or 2147483648) shows a green Voucher updated toast while Save turns into Try again and Unsaved changes remains.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, on a new unsaved free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) restricted to one country, reopen Assign countries, uncheck that last country and confirm. The dialog closes but the country remains assigned and the form still says Valid in 1 country, preventing a return to the empty/worldwide selection through that picker.
logicalBugs.rootCause: In VoucherCreatePage, the country modal confirms through assignItem(countries, "countries", onModalClose). useSpecificItemsAssign.handleItemAssign unions incoming items with the current assigned collection; confirming an empty selection adds nothing instead of replacing/clearing the saved draft selection. This is the create-form assignment contract, not the saved-voucher detail setCountryCodes path.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a new unsaved free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with one country selected, reopen Assign countries, deselect that last country and confirm. The country remains assigned after the dialog closes instead of returning the voucher to its unrestricted country selection.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, choosing a date-between filter in the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) list and leaving one bound incomplete can break the list/query instead of keeping the filter incomplete and allowing correction. A half-entered date interval is submitted as though it were a valid filter.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Voucher date filtering calls joinDateTime for each optional bound and passes the pair onward without ensuring both bounds are a complete valid between expression; a half-entered condition reaches the API as an invalid filter.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor’s Vouchers list, choose a date-between filter but leave one bound incomplete before applying it. The list/query fails instead of keeping the unfinished interval available for correction, so an incomplete date range is submitted as a complete filter.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, select a row in the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) list, then change a filter so another voucher occupies that row position. Selection can transfer to the newly displayed voucher, exposing bulk actions against a different record from the one originally selected.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Datagrid selection is reported by row index; handleSelectVouchersIds maps those indexes against the new vouchers array after the filter changes before clearing the old selection, selecting different IDs at the same positions.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, select a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) row in the list, then change a filter so a different voucher appears at the same row position. Selection transfers to that new voucher instead of staying tied to the originally selected record, exposing bulk actions for an unintended voucher.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, at phone width in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s codes section, selecting codes exposes a Delete codes action that overlaps the rows/page-size dropdown. The two controls compete for the same visible space and are difficult to use independently.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Voucher codes table toolbar/pagination retain their horizontal control geometry on narrow screens without reserving width for selected-row deletion actions.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at phone width in a code-redeemable discount voucher’s codes section, select code rows to reveal Delete codes. That action overlaps the rows-per-page dropdown, so the deletion and pagination controls are drawn over one another instead of remaining independently usable.

logicalBugs.description: Saleor’s voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) setup checklist says percentage discounts use one value across sales channels (storefront/currency configurations) even when the editor allows and saves different percentages for individual channels. The guidance describes a restriction the voucher configuration does not enforce.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The setup message hardcodes Percentage discounts use one value across channels, but channel listings retain independent percentageDiscountValue drafts.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor’s voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) setup checklist, read the percentage-discount guidance while different percentages are configured for separate sales channels (storefront/currency configurations). It says one percentage is shared across channels even though the form allows and saves different channel values.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, with a sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) selected and voucher (a discount redeemed using codes)-list Offer sorting active, refreshing the page changes the active sort to Name instead of preserving Offer. The refreshed order therefore no longer reflects the selected offer values.
logicalBugs.rootCause: VoucherList effect calls canBeSorted before selectedChannel resolves; a channel-dependent value sort is treated as unsupported and replaced with DEFAULT_SORT_KEY.
reproductionPaths: On Saleor’s Vouchers list with a sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) selected, choose Offer sorting and refresh. The active sort changes to Name instead of preserving Offer, so the refreshed rows are no longer ordered by their channel discount values.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, a very small positive sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) percentage, such as 0.000001, is accepted and saved without a precision warning but reopens as 0. The voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) can remain Active although its accepted visible discount was silently rounded away.
logicalBugs.rootCause: VoucherChannelListing.discount_value has fixed DEFAULT_DECIMAL_PLACES while percentage validation checks the maximum but not precision/minimum representable nonzero amount, so storage rounds a finer value.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, for a code-redeemable discount voucher’s sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) percentage, enter a positive value finer than the stored precision and Save. No precision warning is shown, but reopening displays zero instead of the accepted nonzero discount, silently removing the effective offer.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, at phone width, the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) list’s pinned Name column takes nearly the whole grid viewport. Horizontal scrolling cannot expose other columns in a readable width because the desktop-sized pinned column stays in place.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared Datagrid defaults freezeColumns to 1 while the voucher first column keeps desktop width; at phone width it consumes nearly the entire scrolling viewport.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at phone width, open the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) list and scroll its data grid horizontally. The pinned Name column keeps nearly the entire screen width, leaving too little space to read the other columns even when scrolling to them.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, a code-redeemable discount voucher’s Redemptions card can say "Redeemable now" when the voucher has no assigned sales channels (storefront/currency configurations) or no voucher codes. Its schedule is active, but the displayed availability claim ignores the missing prerequisites for redemption.
logicalBugs.rootCause: formatScheduleStatus derives Redeemable now solely from scheduleData; codesCount and channelsCount are shown separately but do not gate that claim.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, after removing all of a code-redeemable discount voucher's sales channels (storefront/currency configurations) or deleting all its codes, the Redemptions card still says 'Redeemable now', while the same page's checklist says the voucher can't be redeemed.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, leaving a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) detail page open across its start or end time does not update the displayed schedule/availability status. A scheduled voucher can remain Scheduled after it starts, or an ended voucher can remain Active until another refresh/render occurs.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getVoucherSchedulePhase evaluates Date.now only when React renders. No timer/subscription schedules a render at start/end, so status remains stale on an otherwise idle page.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on an open voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) detail page, the header status, the Schedule card label and the sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) dot do not change when the scheduled start or end time passes. After the start time it still said "Scheduled · in 2 minutes". After the end time it still said Active, with a green Channel-USD dot. Refreshing the page shows the correct phase each time.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, saving a negative sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) percentage can display Voucher updated while the edited negative value remains on screen, yet reopening the voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) shows the previous discount instead of the reported successful change.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Accepted report retained, but the exact failure path is unresolved: the detail handler submits channel values through updateChannels and aggregates its errors, while normal unsigned input filtering prevents many negative entries. The reported visible -0.01 and successful toast need execution evidence to establish which accepted value and error payload reached the handler. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), enter a negative sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) percentage and Save. A Voucher updated notification appears while the edited negative value remains visible, but a fresh editor shows the previous saved percentage instead of the apparent successful update.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, clearing one segment of an explicitly configured voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) start or end date can save an empty native date value as if the entire optional date were unset. A future start can become immediate activation, or a saved expiration can be removed, without asking the admin to complete the partial date.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DiscountDates forwards date input onChange values without retaining the distinction between an incomplete native date and an intentionally empty date. joinDateTime returns null for a falsy date; the update handler sends that null for startDate/endDate, invoking the API default or clearing expiry. No partial-date validity guard is visible at this boundary. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with an enabled expiry, clear one segment of End Date while leaving other date segments visible, then Save. The expiry is removed and Set end date turns off instead of rejecting the visibly incomplete date.

In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with a future start, clear one segment of Start Date and Save. The incomplete date is treated as unset and replaced with the current start date/time, activating the voucher instead of requiring the partial date to be completed.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, a code-redeemable discount voucher’s multi-sales channel (a storefront/currency configuration) discount editor advertises pasting a spreadsheet column to fill percentages down the channel list. Pasting valid newline-separated percentage values into the first field can leave both the first and subsequent channel values unchanged, without an error explaining why the promised fill-down did not happen.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Exact cause unresolved. VoucherFixedAmountChannelList explicitly captures paste, sanitizes percentage cells and applies the resulting rows via onChannelsChange, so a missing percentage paste handler is not supported. The event target, clipboard payload or propagation into the owning channel state must be checked for the reported setup. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: On a Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with several sales channels (storefront/currency configurations), paste a valid newline-separated column of percentages into the first channel’s percentage field. Neither channel value updates, despite the displayed instruction that spreadsheet values fill down the channel list.

logicalBugs.description: Saleor’s Eligible products section of a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) shows descriptions beside counts of assigned items. At tablet width, the unassigned Products row’s “None assigned” count overlaps its description instead of using a separate readable area, making the row difficult to read before any products are assigned.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The catalogue row header uses a three-column grid with a shrinkable description and nonshrinking metadata/count. This is the source layout boundary for the overlap; whether typography or a breakpoint defeats that intended separation has not been independently reproduced, so the exact CSS failure remains unresolved. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, at tablet width, open a Products-scope voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with no assigned products and inspect its Eligible products rows. The None assigned count overlaps the Products description instead of occupying a separate readable area.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with unsaved edits, use browser Back and choose Keep editing, then use Back again and choose Ignore changes. The warning closes, but the same edited voucher and unsaved-state banner remain on screen instead of discarding the changes and leaving the editor.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The exit-dialog provider handles a cancelled POP by pushing a duplicate current location, and continues an ignored transition by pushing the stored destination rather than replaying the original POP. A following Back can therefore target the duplicate same-page entry, leaving the mounted form intact instead of leaving/discarding it. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, edit a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) name without saving, use browser Back and choose Keep editing, then use Back again and choose Ignore changes. The warning closes but the voucher editor still shows the pending name and unsaved state instead of discarding the edit and leaving the page.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, adding a manual voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) code padded with spaces bypasses the dialog’s duplicate check and creates another draft row. Saving then fails because backend normalization identifies it as the existing code.
logicalBugs.rootCause: voucherCodeExists compares the raw draft code with strict string equality, while the API cleans code whitespace before duplicate validation. The client does not apply that canonicalization before accepting a manual code, so space-padded equivalents are admitted locally but rejected on Save.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, while creating a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), add a unique manual code, then add the same code with surrounding spaces. The dialog accepts the padded duplicate as another draft row, but Save rejects the normalized duplicate rather than catching it during code entry.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, on a saved free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), change the discount scope away and back, then edit and save its assigned countries, including selecting all and subsequently clearing them. Save can report Voucher updated while General settings remains marked unsaved, rather than clearing the warning after the completed save.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The country selection is held in the catalogue draft, merged into the update payload, then reset and refetched after an aggregate successful save. This reset/refetch versus form-initial reconciliation boundary is a candidate for retained dirty state, but the specific race or unreconciled field in the reported sequence has not been established. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved free-shipping voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), switch away from and back to that scope, assign all countries and save, then clear the country selection and save again. Voucher updated appears, but General settings remains marked unsaved instead of becoming clean after the successful update.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, saving a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) start in an ancient year can reopen on the preceding day at 11:59 PM instead of the selected midnight, and the shifted value persists without a warning.
logicalBugs.rootCause: joinDateTime converts local date/time through moment.format before sending it to the API, and the return path splits the stored instant back into local date/time. Historical timezone offsets and their serialized precision are a plausible boundary for the sub-minute shift, but the exact timezone/database roundtrip responsible is not proven from this code alone. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: On a Saleor voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) schedule in a non-UTC timezone, enter a very early calendar year with a midnight start and save it. The displayed and reloaded result shifts to the preceding day just before midnight without warning, instead of preserving the accepted date/time or rejecting an unsupported historical date.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor’s voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) schedule, after a space-padded duplicate draft code fails to save, removing that draft can restore the saved code list and disable Save while leaving its Promo code already exists error visible.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Code removal updates local draft rows, but the API errors supplied to VoucherCodesCard are the previous mutation response. Removing a local code does not reset that response, so a now-inapplicable duplicate error can remain when no further changed value exists to resubmit. This source mechanism does not change the explicit acceptance of this report despite other rejected clear-on-edit preferences. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, on a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes), add a space-padded duplicate code and Save to produce a duplicate-code error, then remove that unsaved draft row. The code list returns to its saved state and Save disables, but the removed code’s error remains visible instead of clearing.

logicalBugs.description: Saleor’s Vouchers list offers a Started greater-than filter with a date and time cutoff. A voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) that started just before that cutoff can remain listed, even though it should be excluded by the chosen time. The failure concerns the time-of-day boundary, rather than a voucher merely sharing the selected calendar date.
logicalBugs.rootCause: getFilterVariables constructs started.gte/lte using joinDateTime(params.startedFrom/startedTo) without a time argument, which defaults to midnight. This can reduce a date-time cutoff to a date-only boundary; the exact serialized URL input in the report remains unverified. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, give a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) a verified start time, then filter the Vouchers list for Started greater than a time one minute later. The voucher remains in the results even though its start is before the chosen cutoff instead of after it.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, deleting a voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) with unsaved edits can succeed on the server and show Voucher deleted, then interrupt the redirect with a Leave without saving changes dialog that offers Keep editing for the deleted voucher.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The delete mutation completion calls navigate(voucherListUrl()) without resetting or suspending the dirty form’s exit guard. Unlike normal form submission, this destructive mutation does not clear the editor dirty state before navigation, so the global blocker can prompt after successful deletion.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, edit a saved voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) without saving, then delete it through More actions and confirm. The server deletion succeeds and Voucher deleted appears, but a Leave without saving changes dialog interrupts the return to the list and still offers Keep editing for the deleted voucher.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, if a successfully deleted voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) remains open after choosing Keep editing, Save offers Try again and tells the admin to check highlighted fields even though the failure is that the voucher no longer exists and no field is marked invalid.
logicalBugs.rootCause: notifySaveFailed selects a codes/catalogue/countries recovery message only for those field errors; all other failures use checkHighlightedFields. A not-found/deleted-object error therefore falls into field-correction copy with no specific missing-object navigation or recovery. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, after deleting a dirty voucher (a discount redeemed using codes) successfully, choose Keep editing in the exit warning and return to the stale editor. Clicking Save offers Try again and says to check highlighted fields even though none are highlighted, instead of explaining that the voucher was deleted and can no longer be saved.

logicalBugs.description: In Saleor, in a saved code-redeemable discount voucher’s product-assignment dialog, choose an Attribute filter, select an attribute value, and apply the filter. The entire voucher editor is replaced by an unexpected-error page instead of the product picker showing matching items or an empty result. This filter-triggered crash is separate from confirming an item assignment on a newly created voucher.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The assignment dialog serializes its conditional filters through useModalFilters and passes the generated product where or collection filter/channel variables to the parent search query. The accepted crash occurs at this filter-application boundary, but no recorded stack or independently confirmed failing statement establishes its exact cause. Keep the product-attribute and collection-publication crashes separate until a common source failure is demonstrated. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: In Saleor, in a saved code-redeemable discount voucher’s product-assignment dialog, choose an Attribute filter, select an attribute value, and apply the filter. The entire voucher editor is replaced by an unexpected-error page instead of the product picker showing matching items or an empty result. This filter-triggered crash is separate from confirming an item assignment on a newly created voucher.
